land.text: Kasi with 'the city of Varanasi' as capital, bounded in the north by 'the Sarpika or Syandika river' (against Kosala) and by 'the river Son' in the south and east (against Magadha); the Cliopatria Kasi disc north-west of Varanasi plus 70 km around the city; 'The Kasi kingdom covered an area of 300 leagues' is a length, not an area

successors.note: The same state: the sa-01-b dossier keeps Cliopatria's Kasi disc for the single year -600 and hands it to janapada-of-kosala ('Conquered by Kaṃsa of Kosala: c. 600 BCE'). One hue for the chain (rule 2).

capitals.note: 'The capital of Kasi was the city of Varanasi'. The page gives no dates for the seat; the span is the state's life. Coordinates are the city's.

ledger.note: c. 1375 BCE: the Kasi kingdom, with Varanasi as its capital. Infobox 'c. 1375 BCE - c. 600 BCE'; the Kasikas 'were first mentioned in the Paippalada recension of the Atharvaveda'; 'During the 9th century BCE, the king of Kasi was Asvasena, the father of the 23rd Jain Tirthankara, Parshvanatha'. The 1375 date is in the infobox only (the body text does not state it), and the whole early life is traditional.

ledger.note: c. 600 BCE: Kosala under Kamsa conquers Kasi. Infobox 'Conquered by Kamsa of Kosala' and 'c. 600 BCE'; 'Kasi was finally conquered for good by Kosala under the latter's king Kamsa'; 'a full part of the kingdom of Kosala by the time of the Kausalya king Mahakosala'. The kingdom passes to the one-year janapada-of-kasi row, then to Kosala (janapada-of-kosala).

certainty.note: A Vedic and Buddhist-era kingdom; the page gives rivers and a capital, and its dates are infobox dates.

sources.title: Kashi Kingdom
sources.note: Infobox c. 1375-c. 600 BCE, capital Varanasi, bounds by the Sarpika and the Son, Asvasena in the 9th century BCE, Kosala's conquest under Kamsa, 300 leagues (a length).

notes: Written from the Kasi infobox date that sa-01-b did not draw ('Established c. 1375 BCE'); the page's body does not state it. The only dated sentence between 1375 and 600 is the 9th-century King Asvasena, who moves no land. Kasi's wars with Kosala and Magadha (Pasenadi, Ajatasattu) are after 600 and belong to janapada-of-kosala and the Magadha dossiers. The shape is the Varanasi core (the sa-01-b dossier's), not the river bounds, because the Sarpika/Syandika and Son would need a river band; a gap-filler may widen it. The wikipedia title is the one sa-01-b records (opened here as Kashi_Kingdom, which loaded the same article).
